【文章原文节选】: Security advisory: openssh-server password authentication bypass | Alpine Linux About Downloads Releases Community Sponsors Donate docs wiki git issues packages mirrors security Small. Simple. Secure. Alpine Linux is a security-oriented, lightweight Linux distribution based on musl libc and busybox. 2026-11-05 Security advisory: openssh-server password authentication bypass If you run sshd on Alpine Linux, update openssh now and restart sshd . Upgrading the package alone does not replace the running daemon. If you cannot update yet, at least disable password logins: set PasswordAuthentication no in your sshd configuration and restart sshd . Either one closes the hole. What is the problem? An attacker who can reach your SSH port can log in without knowing any password. It takes one connection, works every time, and needs no retries. The attacker needs the name of an account whose password field is * (an account with no password set, which is normal for key-only accounts), and needs the machine to have at least one other account with a $5$ or $6$ password hash. The attacker then sends a very long password (257 to 1024 bytes). One user with a password is enough: it makes every account
